repairs.value: Strongest feature: Sechler circumscribes his position, acknowledging annihilationism as more plausible while presenting Lewis's internally locked hell only as a defensible interpretation of eternal conscious torment, demonstrating responsible calibration behind the 93 charity score. Principal limitation: His psychology of finite goods becoming self-destructive remains asserted rather than demonstrated, making the 59 evidential-warrant score understandable despite presentation. Live burden: Sechler needs to explain why misordered attachment persists beyond divine correction, increased understanding, or rehabilitative opportunity, especially when his hesitation concedes serious difficulties for the model. Locked score: The 78 appropriately recognizes engagement with hell's compatibility with divine love while withholding stronger credit because the mechanism connecting freely preferred goods to irreversible, everlasting ruin remains philosophically and theologically insufficiently established.

Strongest feature: Clifton challenges Sechler's locked-from-inside account by comparing permission of everlasting self-destruction with a parent's obligation to interrupt catastrophic decisions, directly supporting the 93 responsiveness score. Principal limitation: The analogy assumes divine love entails parental intervention duties, so the 71 evidential-warrant score reflects uncertainty about whether rescue overrides freedom or responsibility. Live burden: Clifton needs to specify when protective intervention becomes morally mandatory and why divine knowledge and power eliminate differences between parental restraint and God's treatment of enduring rejection. Locked score: The 86 rewards a focused challenge to passive permission of eternal torment, while reserving higher marks because the parental comparison expresses moral intuition without establishing the precise obligations perfect love must satisfy.
